cases.assertion: Return ordered, outer-stripped original fragments without delimiter semicolons; preserve internal spacing, accept a final undelimited statement, ignore empty fragments, and leave input unchanged.

Protect semicolons in ordinary strings, doubled string quotes, doubled quoted identifiers, and uppercase/lowercase escape strings; ordinary backslashes do not escape closing quotes. Region-looking text inside quotes remains literal.
An E/e embedded in identifiers, including accented and dollar-containing identifiers, cannot enable backslash escaping; an E/e after an opening parenthesis can.
Preserve semicolons and misleading comment/string delimiters inside untagged and legal ASCII tagged dollar bodies; mismatched-case and other dollar tags cannot close the body.
Dollar sequences embedded in unquoted identifiers, positional parameters, and invalid tag-shaped sequences cannot begin dollar-quoted regions.

Nested block comments and CR/LF/EOF line comments protect semicolons, remain in statement fragments, and are ignored when they form the entire fragment. Quotes and dollars inside a comment have no meaning.
Unterminated strings, escape strings, identifiers, dollar bodies and nested block comments raise ValueError with the required 'Unterminated SQL' prefix.

Real PostgreSQL executes quoted identifiers/literals, an escape-string-containing function body, a DO body, and nested comments; an execution recorder proves each of five resulting statements is sent separately, with one bootstrap and one file commit.

A real division-by-zero failure rolls back prior inserts and CREATE TABLE effects within its file, excludes that filename from the isolated ledger, preserves the preceding file's committed data, and permits a repaired file on rerun.
A later unterminated dollar quote causes the required ValueError before even the valid first statement in that file reaches PostgreSQL; earlier files and their ledger rows stay committed.

Immediate SQL files execute in filename order with UTF-8 content; nested SQL and non-SQL files are ignored. Empty/comment-only files receive ledger rows and per-file commits. Replay skips by filename even after an applied file is changed to malformed SQL, with no data duplication; console output remains present.
The runner retains exactly one public parameter named migrations_dir, whose default is None.

limitations: No candidate implementation was inspected or executed; only test syntax and design-to-function correspondence were checked before freezing.
Default-path discovery is checked through the public optional-directory signature rather than modifying the candidate's built-in migration directory.
The exact pre-existing console message wording was not provided; the suite checks that console summaries remain present.
Grammar validation, COPY streams, transaction-control SQL, psql commands, non-ASCII dollar tags, concurrency and checksums are outside the required scope.
